concerns.message: Acceptance 2 wants each lane sorted in advance "from its geometry" (enters the unpinched neighbourhood or not), listed by heading and offset only, with the count of lanes that enter matching the prediction exactly. On the sweep's own island (dock (9,7); land at cols 4-9, rows 4-7; hull 80; maxSpeed 39), the ship's real path is not the straight line. Two things break the match. (a) Sliding: a heading-24 lane whose closest point lies over land (e.g. near (2161,1649)) runs into the east face of land tile (9,4)/(9,5). It is blocked on x only, so it slides south along x=2640 into (10,6) and moors. A straight-line classifier puts that lane in "doesn't enter", yet it moors, so the exact count is off. (b) Step sampling: lanes that clip a corner of an unpinched diagonal tile such as (10,6)'s north-east corner can spend less than 39 sub-units inside it. Whether a step starts inside then depends on the start speed (0, half or full). A list keyed by (heading, offset) alone cannot express that. The only classifier that matches exactly would re-run the sail/sweep logic, which is circular. That is the kind of weak sweep the coverage reviewer blocked last time.
concerns.consequence: The worker either loses the 90-minute budget on count mismatches, or ships a classifier that replays the simulation (or quietly narrows offsets to avoid grazing lanes). Either way the coverage reviewer blocks the sweep again, and this follow-up run exists only to fix that sweep.

concerns.message: The claim that at a 384 reach "the neighbourhood already covers the reach disc" is off by one. The neighbourhood spans centre-384 up to (but not including) centre+384 on each axis, while dockInReach accepts distance² ≤ 384². So the points (centre.x+384, centre.y) and (centre.x, centre.y+384) are in reach but in column/row tileX+2 or tileY+2, outside the neighbourhood. The fallback rule can therefore moor there before the ship "enters" the neighbourhood.
concerns.consequence: A sweep lane (e.g. heading 32 at offset 0, if the offset grid includes 0) that happens to land on one of these points moors one step before its predicted "first step inside". The test fails, or the classifier gains an unexplained special case.

concerns.message: "Never end aground within one tile of the berth" doesn't say how distance is measured. As Chebyshev tile distance ≤ 1, the check is empty: any ship stopped in the unpinched neighbourhood with E held moors by construction. The review's real complaint was a ship grounded about 395 sub-units from the berth centre, which calls for a Euclidean bound.
concerns.consequence: The assertion can pass without ever showing that no ship strands visibly beside the dock. A reviewer can't tell whether the dead zone was ruled out or just defined away.

concerns.message: The sweep runs only on the synthetic corner island. The dead zone was found at real south docks like (23,27), which have an inside-corner coastline: land one row north running east. The real-map test at simulation.test.ts:559 covers only headings N-1 and N-2 from the east.
concerns.consequence: A real dock with a different shape (land on both flanks, shoals near the berth, a pinched diagonal) could still have a dead zone that the synthetic sweep never exercises.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Drop the up-front classification from straight-line geometry. Check the property at every step against an oracle that uses only terrain lookups, not dockInReach: from the step's start (x, y), take the tile (floor(x/256), floor(y/256)); it is the berth or an orthogonal neighbour, or a diagonal neighbour with at least one shared tile navigable, or the berth centre is within the reach with a clear run. For every lane (heading every 8 units × start speeds 0, half, full × offsets across ±dockRadius, nothing skipped), assert the ship moors on the first step whose start the oracle accepts. A lane that never gets there must end with its final position more than a stated Euclidean distance from the berth centre (e.g. > 1.5 tiles). Record the lanes that never moor as an exact hard-coded list of (heading, offset, speed), and assert both classes are non-empty. Lanes that slide into the neighbourhood and grazing corners are then handled correctly without re-implementing the sailing physics, and the count is still exact and floor-free. Optionally run the same loop over every dock in the real map with open sides.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: About 15 minutes in a scratch vitest file. Add the adjacency rule plus pinch guard to a local copy of dockInReach. Run today's sweep with the `continue` removed and offsets every 16 across ±384. For each (heading, offset, speed), log two things: whether the straight line from the start first reaches an unpinched neighbourhood tile before any blocked tile, and whether the simulation moored. If any lane disagrees (expect heading 24 lanes sliding down the east face of (9,4)/(9,5), and lanes grazing a corner of (10,6) or (8,8)), or the same (heading, offset) gives different outcomes at different speeds, then the wording \"classified from geometry, listed by heading and offset, exact match\" can't hold and should be replaced by the per-step oracle before any worker starts.
